item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique. It won't be just found footage, the first part of the article is a description of the current situation in Bosnia. Because of the presence of other GOI and the over all danger that the war poses to Foundation personnel all sites in the former Yugoslavia have been evacuated, and the anomalies have been transferred to other European sites. The MTF extraction of Bojana was sort of a last minute thing. While waiting for Kosta, Bojana goes through short examinations, which are described in the archives of the site.
Second part goes through the investigation of the clashes that occurred. Third part is found footage from the body armor and the Foundation vehicle that Kosta took. There are some diary entries in-between the scenes.

item.title: Re: SCP Draft: The Place I Belong
item.content:encoded:
Hey, Grig! I'll take a look for ya!

Just know that my clinical tone is meh, but I'm a lot better with dialogue.

Alrighty.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Disinformation campaigns are to be spearheaded to label SCP-XXXX-A as a UNESCO World Friendship and Peace Village to draw in more tourism.

The fact that a ConProc demands more attention is already weird enough to draw me in.
I dig it.

SCP-XXXX is a series of anomalous dreams that can occur in a certain segment of the population of Europe and Asia: most often creatives and individuals who attest to feeling at odds with society.

I feel personally called out here and I'm not sure how to mentally process this.

I just finished the Description and I don't really have any qualms with it. The dream sequences reminds me heavily of the River Styx and Charon, something I'm not sure if you did on purpose or not.
Either way, no clinical issues so far.

Aside from this:

genius loci

Did you mean 'genus'?

A little confused on that bit. I had to Google 'loci' and it gave me stuff about genetics and mathematics, neither of which this piece seems to be going for. I…actually no clue what this bit is supposed to show.

I'm normally not a fan of free verse (that is what that poetry style is, right?), but the poem written by Tefvik is wonderfully done and the allusions to the hooded figure in the SCP-XXXX dreams is also nicely done.

Especially 'blessed be the stones of your dreaming streets.'

prototypical oneirosensory visualization recording device.

Ironic…we're both currently drafting something that headcanons pioneering dream-recording Foundation tech.

I…don't know how to process this either.

I do think this is great headcanon, and I think your method of wording this is a lot better and a lot more developed than mine.

Dr. Rossi has confirmed that she is experiencing SCP-XXXX events and has been periodically for the previous three weeks.

We can clean this up and shorten it into, 'Dr. Rossi has confirmed that she has been periodically experiencing SCP-XXXX events for the previous three weeks.'

[ Initial view is of a mist shrouded body of water, which appears to be a river. The night is dark, with only a crescent moon serving as illumination.]

Unnecessary extra space before 'Initial' and after the bracket.

[The boat has stopped directly in front of subject in a manner inconsistent with the flowing water of the river, as if being held in place. The figure extends his arm out with an open palm.]

I love dream logic. This is a lovely detail to show how unearthly this place is. Other than, you know, the weird hooded figure, the mist and—
You know what I mean.

Sixteen minutes of footage are lost due to technical failure.

Both of our headcanoned dream-recording technology also involves significant lapses in dream recording to simulate the feeling of actual dream timeline-logic.

That's…frighteningly coincidental.

I love it. Love it, love it, love it <3

[Subject is within the village, walking down its streets. The stone buildings resemble architecture from the 18the century

There's an extra 'e' in '18th'

Rossi: The air is chilly, like an early spring night but not so cold as to be uncomfortable. Significant moisture in the air, consistent with misty conditions. The river in front of me is jet black, I cannot tell how deep it is by eye. I –”

This is very prose-y instead of diaogue-y (if that makes sense), but this is a dream and we could say she is trying to ground herself in a world where normal logic doesn't function.

[Sounds of a scuffle and Rossi cursing loudly cursing.]

Two 'cursing's here.

Removing either would fix it, funny enough.

Many instances8 of SCP-XXXX-1 are seen lining the square and staring at subject.]

There has been no mention of SCP-XXXX-1 up until this point, so I don't know what they're supposed to be.

Subject stands in a town square, the cobble stones shifting beneath her feet.

I absolutely adore the usage of dream logic and dream visuals here.

Answers don’t come in dreams at least not for you.

Comma after 'dreams'. Unless you're going for a sort of mysterious thing where the run on sentences show how unearthly this being is.

Also, odd how its dialogue switches to a different, bolded and italcized style here wheras earlier, it spoke like this.

Also, earlier, it was addressed as Unknown, whereas here, there's no addressing as such.

Maybe I'm just a stickler for consistency, I don't know, but I found this a tad jarring.

Wrong

No period.

Rossi: What are you talking about?

I personally imagine this character responding with 'What you do mean 'wrong?'' as a way to sass it. Can't explain why.

I just finished the first Addendum.

Hmmm…so far, I find the dialogue pretty decent. There's a good sense of mystery and a good sense of buildup, but I don't feel attached to Rossi. She feels like she's just there.

Also, the hooded figure feels a little too 'generic mysterious dream person' to me.

Like, I really dig it all, but it's missing a little bit of that pizzazz which makes me go from nodding my head and approving to making the following face:

:o

And losing all breath at the insane BS occuring before me.

Descriptions are lovely, though and the use of dream logic is very good. A little too downplayed, though, in my opinion; it's a dream and yet, despite lapses in timeline and everything being misty and hard to make out with shadowy figures, it doesn't get weird enough in my opinion. The weirdest we see is the dream figure levitating and twirling in the air. It's a dream and I think the surreal nature can be cranked up a notch or 12.

Then again, I can see that that isn't what you're really going for, so this part can be taken however you wish.

Personally, I just love seeing dream logic become as surreal and weird as possible. Probably just me.

11. There is no body of water within twenty kilometers of Kayaköy.

I like this touch here to show the difference between the 'real' version and the dream version.

Waltham: I can get to the edge of town, it’s not infinite… but then I’ll blank and it will fold in on itself; fall apart until it reforms and I’m sent right back to the fucking church..

Lovely dream logic. Sorry I'm being a broken record, I just really love weird things.

Waltham: I’m not alone here. I thought I was, but I’m not. There’s something here. I haven’t seen anything but… I’m being watched.

This feels a tad too rehearsed.

Waltham: I'll be the judge of that. I said, come out where I can see you.

You are looking right at me. Do you like it?

Needs a space between the two.

The street and buildings are also exhibiting non-Euclidean geometrics as they fold in upon themselves, shifting the camera between different elevations and rapidly restructuring from one layout to another.

This. I personally would like more stuff like this. That said, I'm having a difficult time imagining all of this. Then again, describing non-euclidean geometry is very difficult, so I'm not really sure what else to offer here.

Personally, this makes me think of the video game Control when I imagine the walls moving. Same with the streets.

Do you like it this way?

[Waltham does not respond. She is believed to be unconscious.]

Oh.

So the thing has a clumsy side. I…don't really like this scene. To me, this moment feels almost Tom and Jerry-ish in a piece that's meant to feel melancholy and strange.

And there’s no one else… You have to stay!

This was the twist that gave me chills.

After her debriefing, the current Special Containment Procedures were put in place. To date, no further SCP-XXXX events have occurred.

Well, shit. The hooded figure is just lonely and wants company. Well, that's a twist I wasn't expecting.

Other than that last bit, a good bit of the scenes just felt really rehearsed. The sequence of events were intriguing enough to keep me going and it was built up well and the dialogue was serviceable, but I think I can just summarize it as that:serviceable.

The twist? Fantastic.

I can understand the clumsy moment earlier now. The child-like clinginess and that clumsy moment from earlier, the way it begs for people to stay. It's like a lonely little kid that just wants friends.

That's a great twist.

I just think the journey along the way needs to be patched up.

Rossi and Waltham just feel like vehicles to show some weird stuff happenng.

I get the feeling that Rossi is meant to be sassy and strongwilled while Waltham is supposed to be serious and soldier-tough with a soft side, but if that's what you were going for, it doesn't come through enough.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day, Grig!

<3

If you got any questions or I was clumsy and was unclear on a few things, feel free to PM or .tell me!

I'm going to mostly piggy-back off the latter half of what ARD said here.

+ show block
– hide block

To me it feels like the focus of this article is really on Chaz, rather than the establishment or the food. There's not a lot of time spend developing the place, or the narrator, or his relationship to food (or to being a vampire!) beyond a surface-level. There's a lot of groundwork being laid about the rules of vampires, but they're either things that the reader likely already knows (stay out of the sunlight!) or stuff that is glossed over (hospitality rites). This seems confusing at first, but I think it's supposed to set our expectations for Chaz himself.

The issue then is twofold. One, the reveal that Chaz isn't a vampire falls really flat. In the article we actually spend very little time getting to know Chaz - he doesn't show up till, like, 70% through, and then he's not actually present for the hunt. So the reveal doesn't really land as meaningful because the article doesn't present Chaz as anything other than "chef who is a vampire".

The second issue is that this article is clearly intended to be a part of a greater whole. And in that lens, as ARD points out above, I feel like we actually don't learn anything about Chaz that wasn't already well established - he's cannibal Elon Musk, but for restaurants.

an entire race of people defined by the need to eat.

I think Chaz is the least interesting part about Ambrose, personally. Vampires are frequently defined by hedonism, but what does a hedonist who no longer can experience pleasures of the flesh look like? I would love to see a version of this article that really drills down on the thoughts and perspectives of an immortal vampire who cannot eat, and his relationship to food, time, pleasure, and the experience of being. What would it be like for someone to taste something for the first time in 3 centuries? How does that experience change someone?

Hello hello Dr Ivan Hext and welcome to the Wiki! I'm a site author and member of the Community Outreach Team, and this comment is a little info list of resources that will hopefully help you with your journey through the site. We're very happy to see new people excited about writing for the Wiki like you. :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting.

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey!

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing! Take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.content:encoded:
Greenlight - YES
SCP Article
Horror/ Psychological Horror
Layout - Standard Scip article
*Tunnel To Your Childhood*
Elev Pitch - A migrating tunnel that manifests in tunnels where tragedies have occurred, when entered humans will see something from their childhood, something they always associated with good memories. This memory will manifest itself into a twisted physical form, and attack the victim. I want to have several MTF encounters and maybe a tale in the future about one encounter

Central - I want to have this be a staple in reality-bending SCP's and I'm going to work hard on this article, and I'm going to write some SCP's that link to this one in a way I haven't decided yet, and create a complex world of memory changers and reality benders

Hook - My article is going to be creating horrific visages of your favorite childhood memories, and I would appreciate your memories to be used for my article, and I'll do my damndest to make it worthy of a phobia.

Thank you to those reading, and please comment some memories for me to put a sick twist in :)

item.title: Re: Recommend a Canon
item.content:encoded:
And so, I thought I'd ask what canons individual members would recommend for a starting point to a guy who mostly read random SCPs and Tales until now?

What are your interest when reading through SCP articles? Do you prefer heartwarming, horror, what?

Recommend a Canon

Well, off the top of my head, I would definitely name off Rat's Nest and The Man Who Wasn't There.

WHY you recommend it?

Rat's Nest: Take's common GoI's and shifts their perspectives in interesting and believable ways. Covers a very unique take on "The end of the world." Very engaging story, many unique entries. They all cover unique topics, and even within the canon, there is no "canon" pre se. You can read in any order you wish, and still get the topics. Very well made canon hub, and has some very interesting entries to boot. One in particular I would recommend from this canon is 1. This may be in the last era of the canon, but it covers many GoI's, as well as skips, meaning no matter what your interest are, you'll likely find something you like in this tale.

The Man Who Wasn't There: Quite the interesting concept, and the canon allows much more expansion then the GOI. Very interesting takes in all directions, and the way it was set up is some of the best. I'd especially recommend the more recent entries from canrencon, more specifically, The Man In The White Suit. Very interesting perspectives, and an engaging storyline.

item.title: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.content:encoded:
So, I think the Serpent's Hand would be better to be a part of / work for than the SCP Foundation. Here are all my points, in no particular order:

1. Foundation operates out of boringly-decorated, overly sanitary-looking research facilities filled with deadly monsters that can get loose at any second, not to mention they are constantly raided by the Chaos Insurgency. The Serpent's Hand gets a frikin' extradimensional library that requires actual frikin' magic to access, and is actually very safe because all of the anomalies within are friendly as long as nobody gets violent against them or breaks the rules. Nice place to chill and relax, maybe play some Dungeons and Dragons and write in peace.

2. Foundation deprives anomalous humans of their humanity, and instead locks them up in basically prison (I don't give a crap about how much you think Iris Thompson likes it there, she most likely secretly hates being locked up, along with literally any other human SCP).

3. They fight for the rights of law-abiding anomalous humans that just want to go about their lives without having to worry about being either imprisonated by the SCP Foundation, murdered by the Global Occult Coalition, weaponized by the Chaos Insurgency, or sold by MC&D. Basically, they tell everybody else to chill their heels and leave anomalous people the heck alone. Which is actually a pretty noble cause. The only reason they raid Foundation / GoC locations is because that is one of the only ways to get their points across. Plus, they do stealth missions, and kill Foundation personnel in only a limited capacity.

4. The Serpent's Hand doesn't breach dangerous anomalies for no good reason at all. That's the Chaos Insurgency's job, after all. If the Serpent's Hand doesn't have a good reason to breach any given SCP during a raid, they won't breach said SCP. They do, however, steal Safe SCP items, and let peaceful human SCPs to escape. They may even attempt to free D-class if possible. They're not stupid, and they don't want to bring about the end of the world by releasing highly dangerous Euclid, Keter, and Apollyon SCPs. Again, that is the Chaos Insurgency's job.

5. Simply existing as a worker on a Foundation site means that you are alive on moment, and then the next you are dead due to being freakin' eaten by a massive lizard that is literally too angry to die or turned into a zombie by a dude cosplaying as a medieval plague doctor, and your friends and family will be unaware of your death (if all of them are outside of the foundation, which is most likely). If you do manage to survive through the containment breach, you will still be mentally scarred by the experience. As I said earlier, the Serpent's Hand operates out of a peaceful library, with a 0% chance of being eaten by a bloodthirsty monster.

6. I also believe that the serpent's hand probably is one of the morally better GoIs, considering their entire mission statement is "we want rights for anomalous humans, and knowledge about the paranormal should be public." While they do break the law from time to time (which would make them Chaotic or Neutral Good), they don't do so for no reason at all. They just want the world to be a better place.

item.title: Re: The Three Sided Coin
item.content:encoded:
I don't think the focus on 'Mr. Exolia' works for me here; particularly since it seems to rely entirely on him being humorous, which is super hard to pull off in text. In part it's also cos he doesn't really…do anything? He doesn't feel like a protagonist driving the story forward and in part that's because there's not really a story being driven forward? There's no-one here making choices that affect the outcome here and it feels….lacking as a result?

This is a very bare bones description I've written here to fit within the forums parameters. There is more detail to the story in which Exolia sets up some difficult decisions for the foundation site staff. Its in my sandbox if you'd like to take a look.

There's also not really a sense of characters grow: they change somewhat throughout, but only when the story forces them to (e.g., the gambling and losing causes Exolia to become a monster, there's no personal transition from happy funny chill dude to anger because it's forced by the coin; then later he gets withdrawal symptoms but it feels unearned because he didn't choose to give up the coin).

I'm not sure where you're getting that Mr. Exolia is angry from. Exolia's character is pretty consistently witty and upbeat until the coin is taken away. You are correct that the coin causes him to have withdraw symptoms when taken but that is intentional. It is supposed to kinda symbolize the feeling a gambler has when they lose everything and can no longer play the game. Thats essentially the idea behind this whole thing, its supposed to represent the dangers of gambling addiction.

The change of the transformation into a monster being implied to be non-permanent feels weird; though I'm still very unclear on what actually happens when someone is turned into a monster.

So yes, the change is non-permanent. Basically when the coin is bet on and lands on the anomalous side it turns the person who flipped it into a monster who then kills their opponent. Its the springing of a trap that was set up when the person tricked their victim into making a bet with them. Then once the victim is dead/eaten the monster turns back into the person. Its kinda similar to how Pennywise the clown is actually a crazy alien, but he only reveals that when he's devouring someone, then he goes back to being a clown. Once again, I think all of this comes off more complete in my sandbox.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Three Sided Coin

Reading this 4+ years after it came out, I wondered whether this or Good As New came out first. When I realized that it was the latter, I was disappointed that it appeared we were getting a retread of the same basic idea (although "Eye points in the opposite direction of the host's natural eye" becomes much funnier if you imagine it as polar opposite, rather than opposite direction within the socket).

When I got to the video log, I was pleasantly surprised to find that the overall plot of AR1 being moved forward, as the seemingly invincible organization begins to crumble from within. The two letters, particularly Anderson's lack of a closing beyond a signature, were quite well done. It was impressive that none of the characters came across as one-dimensional, even within the constraints of a video log/letter. Since I can't be positive, I will say that the "deal with the devil" line felt a bit trite. Otherwise, though, outstanding work.

Vincent can always find another glorified accountant. But he only has one of me.

Pictured: Words that will not prove bitterly ironic at some point down the road.

Footnotes
1. Still trying to figure out where I fall on the "articles should stand in isolation" scale, but I think that this sidesteps it by being relatively understandable by someone who might not have an idea about the broader Anderson Robotics series.

item.title: The Drag Strip Phantom/The Black Magnum
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard description and event chronology as well as mission reports and test logs

Elevator Pitch: The phantom of a 1970 Chevrolet Camaro that manifests itself on lonely stretches of desert road at night to challenge high-performance passer-by cars to a drag race.

Central Narrative: A rumor spreads in a small town in Colorado about a mysterious "ghost car", originating from a local drag racing enthusiast. According to the legend, the racer encounters the SCP and the road transitions into a foggy, abandoned drag strip - with the stoplight and everything. The Foundation takes note after several others have reported the same occurence and dispatches a team to study the anomaly up-close and personal ("prodding" the car as it appears and exploring the strip dimension), as well as launching an investigation into the car's possible origins. At one point, a GoI will have blown the car up (no clue, which one, yet), after which, basically, Christine happens: Someone finds a junker 1970 Camaro, and with maniacal passion, restores it, builds it and crashes it violently - thus causing the phantom to be "reborn". From then on, the Foundation tries to relocate it to the most deserted stretch of blacktop possible and keep it happy by regularly setting up drag races.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mystery surrounding the car itself: Is it sentient, is it dangerous, what is the drag strip, where does the car come from, is anyone behind the wheel, how can it be contained etc. etc. The origins part only really comes in only before the SCP is "reborn", after which all focus is on active study and containment - origin study is moved to a passive state.

Additional Notes: The drag strip is a separate dimension that flat-out disables digital devices (not electronic)./Cars cannot leave the dimension unless they race or crash, at which point they become part of the SCP./The phantom sustains itself off of life energy gained in the final stage of its "rebirth"./It is sentient and has a memory./It can manifest at will anytime between sunset and dawn./It is not bound to any road in particular and can move at any time.

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post - Info
item.content:encoded:
Hey JamaisJ: the information you have set out here is not accurate; please be mindful of this in future. In particular:

"Central Narrative" is basically what the thing does and a brief history of it. If you're familiar with D&D, this is the monster description of the SCP: What it looks like, its history, and other germaine details. You should also describe what narrative role it fits in the general SCP universe. Use as many words as you want.

'what the thing does' and 'a brief history of it' are not part of the central narrative: the elevator pitch is a better place for 'what the thing does' and the history isn't necessarily necessary in a SCP. The "this is the monster description of the SCP" analogy is also flawed as a result.

More accurately: the Central Narrative section is for the core story of the SCP: it's where you talk about the shape of the article and what you intend to do beyond just describing what the SCP is.

It should be done in about 100 words tops.

Both times you mention '100 words' implies this is a hard limit over a recommendation: while keeping this sections short is a good idea, there's no hard limit on it and in some cases, they can both be longer than the Central Narrative section.

item.title: Re: Eurotrash
item.content:encoded:
I'd love to see more FBI stories that manage to not get bogged down in X-files revanchism.

The key is to develop your main characters in a way that isn't a Mulder and Scully rehash.

So I'll give you the character workshopping template questions:

How are the relations between the characters? Do they like each other?

Are they choleric, sanguine, phlegmatic or melancholic? Are they shy, outgoing?

What is the outcome? How do the characters change because of it? Does the FBI fail to contain this due to ignorance, hubris, bad luck or do they succeed? Do our agents' character flaws lead to that failure or do they prevail in spite of them?
